team.claim: Founders: Melanie Perkins (CEO), Cliff Obrecht (COO) and Cameron Adams (Chief Product Officer); Canva was founded 1 January 2013 in Perth, Australia.

CFO Kelly Steckelberg joined Canva in November 2024; previously CFO of Zoom (took it through IPO), CFO and CEO of Zoosk, and divisional CFO for the Consumer Segment and WebEx at Cisco; began her career at KPMG.

Aggregator (Clay dossier, may lag): other named executives include Zach Kitschke (Chief Marketing Officer), Damien Singh (CFO per the dossier, superseded by Steckelberg) and Todd Carpenter (Chief Legal Officer & Corporate Development).

Four senior leaders left Canva in May 2026 as it repositions as an AI platform: growth lead Iain Dowling resigned after eight years in senior roles and senior engineering director Jonathan Ross was leaving at month end (AFR); secondary reporting names the other two as head of design Andrew Green and CTO Brendan Humphreys, with broader staff concerns about job security.

output.company: Canva, Inc. (Canva — Australian graphic design / visual communications software company, Sydney HQ)

funding.claim: Canva raised about $569 million in primary equity across 11 rounds from 2013 to 2021; the last primary round, $200 million in September 2021 led by T. Rowe Price (with Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis, AirTree), valued it at $40 billion. No new primary money since.

Secondary sales: ~$100M Blackbird sale to Coatue and ICONIQ at $25.5B (Aug 2023); ~$1.6B staff/early-investor sale run by Goldman Sachs at ~$26B (Mar-Apr 2024); secondary trades at $32B (Oct 2024); more than $2 billion of existing shares sold since 2023, none of it going to the company.
In August 2025 Canva ran an employee share sale led by Fidelity with JPMorgan Asset Management participating, pricing Canva at $42 billion (last known secondary-market valuation).
In 2026 investors marked Canva at $34.9 billion to $39.3 billion; Canva's own independent valuation for its August 2026 employee share issue fell about 20% year over year to $31 billion.

IPO status: private, no filing; COO Cliff Obrecht told Bloomberg in November 2025 that Canva will go public in the next 'couple of years' (aggregator reporting says he expects a listing in 2027); Canva ruled out an Australian listing in September 2025.

output.verdict: Canva looks strong on scale and efficiency: 265M+ monthly active users, ~$4B ARR with 100% B2B ARR growth, ~$1.5B in cash, a decade of claimed free-cash-flow profitability, and a CFO hired from Zoom with IPO-readiness in mind. The closer look items are the August 2026 growth-guidance cut (30% to 20%) driven by AI inference costs, the May 2026 cluster of four senior departures including the CTO, a ~20% markdown in Canva's own internal valuation to $31B versus its $42B secondary mark, and customer backlash that forced a reversal of AI-driven price hikes — plus the fact that profitability rests on company claims rather than filed accounts.

business.claim: Canva, Inc. is an Australian multinational private software company founded 1 January 2013 in Perth and headquartered in Sydney, founded by Melanie Perkins, Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams; its platform provides drag-and-drop graphic design for presentations, websites, posters, social media content and photo/video editing.
Canva operates a freemium SaaS model and has added features such as print services and video editing over time.

Canva sells subscription tiers up to Canva Enterprise for large organisations, with API access, two-way DAM sync (Bynder, Widen, Brandfolder), native Salesforce and HubSpot apps, and marketing-automation integrations (Marketo, Eloqua); its site cites a Salesforce case study of 66% lower cost per design with Canva Enterprise.
In May 2024 Canva launched Canva Enterprise, a plan designed for large organisations, alongside Work Kits, Courses and AI capabilities.
Canva operates in over 190 countries and supports over 100 languages, with Canva AI available in 16 languages across 31 locales; the majority of its business is from North America.
Canva's group includes subsidiaries Pixabay, Pexels, Serif (Affinity), Kaleido, Leonardo.AI, Smartmockups, Flourish, Cavalry, MangoAI, Simtheory and Ortto.

In February 2025 Canva reorganised its corporate group: a newly incorporated Delaware company, Canva, Inc., became the group's ultimate holding company; the former parent was registered in Australia as Canva Australia Holdings Pty Ltd.

traction.claim: Company claim: Canva had more than 265 million monthly active users and over 31 million paid users in 2025, with MAU up 20% year over year.
Company claim: annual recurring revenue reached $4 billion by end of 2025, and its B2B business (companies with more than 25 seats) grew 100% to $500 million in ARR, per co-founder/COO Cliff Obrecht.
Aggregator (citing Canva's own materials): Canva says it is trusted by 95% of the Fortune 500; Expedia Group, Airbnb and Salesforce appear among its listed enterprise customers.
Company claim: Canva's AI mini-apps and website builder tool has more than 10 million monthly active users.

Canva is integrated with ChatGPT and Claude; by October 2025 users had logged more than 26 million conversations with the Canva app on ChatGPT, and Canva claimed to be one of the top 10 referred domains from ChatGPT.
Partnerships: Canva announced a partnership with FedEx Office in June 2020 and with Office Depot in July 2020 for print services.

Acquisition spree: Zeetings (2018), Pixabay and Pexels (May 2019), Kaleido.ai and Smartmockups (Feb 2021), Flourish (2022), Serif/Affinity for ~$380 million (March 2024), Leonardo.AI (announced July/August 2024), MagicBrief (June 2025), Cavalry and MangoAI (February 2026), Simtheory and Ortto (April 2026).

On 10 April 2025 Canva released Visual Suite 2 (Canva Sheets, Canva Code, chatbot, updated photo editor); in April 2026 it introduced Canva AI 2.0 in research preview with agentic tools, and in August 2026 an offline mode.

red_flags.claim: Revenue-growth forecast cut by a third (30% to 20%) in August 2026 due to unexpectedly high AI inference/serving costs — the core growth thesis now carries a unit-economics question.
Four senior leaders (including CTO Brendan Humphreys) departed within one month, May 2026, during the AI pivot, amid reported broader staff concerns about job security.

Valuation markdown: Canva's own independent valuation for its August 2026 employee share issue fell ~20% year over year to $31 billion, versus the $42 billion August 2025 Fidelity-led secondary price; 2026 investor marks span $34.9-39.3 billion.
Pricing whiplash: a steep genAI-driven price increase (~4x for a five-person Teams plan) was reversed after small-business and educator backlash, indicating pricing power limits in its core segments.
Legacy security exposure: May 2019 breach of ~137-139 million accounts with ~4 million cracked passwords circulated in January 2020 (historic, but relevant to enterprise-trust diligence).

Australian compliance and disclosure friction: reported A$800,000 fine for late lodgement of financial reports (Herald Sun via Wikipedia, unverified on a primary page), and public commentary that Canva's 'profitable' status is not verifiable from filed accounts because of private-company disclosure gaps.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor (aggregator, as of 2026-10-21): overall rating 4.1/5; category ratings — career opportunities 3.1, work/life balance 3.4, compensation and benefits 3.5, culture & values 3.8, diversity & inclusion 3.8; trend based on 384 reviews in the last 6 months; review summary praises collaborative, inclusive culture but highlights favouritism and a disconnect between leadership and staff.

Customer backlash over genAI pricing: after generative-AI features drove subscription prices up (a five-person annual Canva Teams plan jumped to $500 from $120/year), Canva reversed the price hike and restored legacy pricing for long-standing small-business and education customers (article date not shown on page; retrieved 2026-10-21).
Social sentiment: the Affinity (Serif) acquisition sparked concern and protest sentiment among parts of the Affinity user community on Reddit about Canva's ownership of the professional tool suite.

Critical press: commentary (citing The Aussie Corporate / Capital Brief) frames the May 2026 clustered senior departures, AI-credits business-model shift, delayed IPO and steep AI-linked price rises as signs of strain in the AI pivot.

Primary/registry confirmation of the reported A$800,000 fine for late financial-report lodgement (only via Herald Sun reference cited on Wikipedia)
Formal regulatory action or sanctions-exposure record from regulator dockets (ASIC/ACCC/FTC) — none found in pages opened
Glassdoor CEO approval percentage — not shown on the review page extracted

financial_signals.claim: Company claim (Cliff Obrecht to TechCrunch): $4 billion ARR at end of 2025, including $500 million ARR from 25+ seat B2B customers, up 100%.

Sacra estimate (aggregator): Canva hit $4B ARR at end of 2025, up 43% from $2.8B at end of 2024; Canva's own 2025 recap reported $3.5B in FY2025 revenue, with ARR and recognised revenue diverging due to annual/multi-year contracts.

Company claim (per Revenue Memo): Canva says it has been profitable on a free-cash-flow basis for nine years and held $1.47 billion in cash at end of June 2026 (Sacra separately says 'operating profitably for the past 7 years' — figures conflict).

Headcount: 5,500 employees (2024) per Wikipedia infobox citing AFR; LinkedIn company page shows an employee count range of 1,001-5,000 with 20,019 associated members (as of 2026-10-21); no verified 2026 total headcount found.

Layoffs: one recorded layoff event — 10 employees cut in AI-related job cuts around 2 April 2025 (layoffs.fyi, citing AFR 'Canva shocks employees with AI-related job cuts'); otherwise hiring-positive trend (aggregator citing Canva newsroom: 1,128 new hires in a year, UK team scaled from 100 to 250+, Europe 400+).

In August 2026 Canva cut its expected revenue growth rate by a third, from 30% to 20%, after unexpectedly high AI serving costs; CEO Melanie Perkins said the cost per AI task had fallen nearly 90% since Canva AI 2.0 launched in April, but users were creating three times as many designs, and the company slowed the rollout while rebuilding architecture.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: May 2019 data breach: roughly 137.5 million user records (usernames, names, email addresses, country/city, password hashes, some Google tokens) exposed by hacker GnosticPlayers on 24 May 2019; in January 2020 Canva learned ~4 million stolen passwords had been decrypted and shared online and forced resets for users who had not changed passwords since the breach.
Secondary citation (Wikipedia reference list to Herald Sun; primary not opened): Canva was reportedly hit with an A$800,000 fine for failing to lodge financial reports on time in Australia.
Secondary citation (Wikipedia reference list to AFR, 10 April 2024): Canva agreed to settle an unfair dismissal case brought by a senior engineer.

Tax/regulatory structure: the February 2025 Delaware holding-company restructure was covered by an Australian Taxation Office class ruling (CR 2025/35) on scrip-for-scrip roll-over treatment of stock options, issued 28 May 2025.
No Canva-named AI copyright or IP litigation appears in the AI copyright lawsuit tracker reviewed (Salesforce, Getty v. Stability and others listed; no Canva), as of 2026-10-21.
